elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."; § 12.3 "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete ... commitment"

elements.element: No field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory"; § 12.4 permits competing activity "in any territory"

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a named competing product
elements.evidence: Condition absent — no restriction survives; "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes"

elements.element: Any restriction during the term only
elements.evidence: Condition absent — the twenty-four-month tail is now permissive: "Customer may develop"
Condition absent — no prohibition remains to which a duration cap could attach

elements.element: Carve-out for internal development and acquisitions
elements.evidence: Condition absent — Customer expressly may "develop ... or acquire any product or service"

reasons: The single operator swap ("shall not develop" → "may develop") removes the only compete restriction on Customer, achieving the preferred position of no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
Fallback limiting conditions are vacuously satisfied because no restriction on Customer remains.
Minimal: one short-phrase replacement in § 12.4; no other language touched, no new exceptions or boilerplate added.

Intent preserved: § 12.3 remains effective and § 12.4 as flipped is consistent with it; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics. The residual permissive time framing ("During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter") is harmless surplus, not an operative restriction, and is noted rather than treated as a defect.
